title: KEEPER: Learning Control-Sufficient Textual Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.41482v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recursive textual memory can carry earlier errors into later updates, yet task performance alone does not establish memory reliability. We define self-consistency bias as the persistence of incorrect claims already present in the incoming memory. We present KEEPER, a comparative analysis of four auxiliary objectives along information-content and update-sensitivity axes within a shared recursive interface, examining how supervision targets relate to agent performance. Among evaluated conditions, reward-related prediction achieve the highest task performance before and after offline reinforcement learning, outperforming joint supervision. A claim-level analysis of one baseline trajectory documents error persistence despite corrective observations. Together, these analyses motivate evaluating error persistence and valid-information retention alongside task outcomes.

translated_title: KEEPER：为长时程LLM智能体学习控制充分的文本记忆
translated_abstract: 递归式文本记忆可能会将早期错误带入后续更新中，然而仅凭任务表现并不能确立记忆的可靠性。我们将“自我一致性偏差”定义为传入记忆中已存在的错误断言持续留存的现象。我们提出了KEEPER，在共享的递归接口下，沿信息内容和更新敏感性两个维度对四种辅助训练目标进行了比较分析，考察监督目标与智能体性能之间的关系。在所评估的条件中，与奖励相关的预测在离线强化学习前后均取得了最高的任务表现，优于联合监督。针对一条基线轨迹的断言级分析记录了尽管存在纠正性观察，错误仍然持续存在的现象。这些分析共同表明，应当在任务结果之外，同时评估错误持续性和有效信息保留情况。
tldr: 该论文提出KEEPER框架，在共享递归接口下比较四种辅助训练目标，发现基于奖励相关的预测目标能在离线强化学习前后均取得最佳任务表现，并提出应同时评估记忆的错误持续性与有效信息保留情况。
en_tdlr: KEEPER comparatively analyzes four auxiliary objectives for recursive textual memory in long-horizon LLM agents, showing that reward-related prediction achieves the best task performance before and after offline RL, and motivating evaluation of error persistence and valid-information retention alongside task outcomes.
